(Search snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; CNBC's own reporting language)

Brent crude futures rose 3.1% to $112.20 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude gained 2.79% to $99.86.
Oil prices climbed Thursday on worries over a possible escalation in the Middle East conflict as the U.S. reportedly plans to resume strikes against Iran. The U.S. has also ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, as Houthi attacks against the country rise. The withdrawal order was prompted by fresh attacks from Yemen's Houthi group on Saudi targets, including a civilian airport and an oilfield.
The U.S. and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for renewed Iran strikes after the Nov. 3 midterms.

(Reuters wire, via syndication snippets, earlier ~05:42 BST:) Brent crude futures rose $1.93, or 1.77%, to $110.75 a barrel at 0442 GMT, while WTI gained $1.43, or 1.47%, to $98.58. "Oil prices rose more than $1 a barrel on Thursday after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over a broader escalation of conflict and further disruptions to supplies from the Middle East."
